summary: Contrast methane and water while distinguishing atoms from electron-pair guides.
objective: Compare methane and water in 3D and let me show electron-pair guides separately from atoms.
example_prompts: Compare methane and water in 3D and let me show electron-pair guides separately from atoms.
Rotate water to see why a tetrahedral electron-pair arrangement does not mean four bonded atoms.

entities.name: Atoms and bonds
entities.guidance: Construct each molecule from explicit element IDs, bonds and positions; sticks terminate at atom centers.

entities.name: Lone-pair guides
entities.guidance: Use translucent lobes distinct from atom spheres and include an electron-pair legend.

object_craft.structure: Construct each molecule from explicit element IDs, bonds and positions; sticks terminate at atom centers.
object_craft.material: Conventional labeled element colors; sphere sizes are display radii.

object_craft.structure: Use translucent lobes distinct from atom spheres and include an electron-pair legend.
object_craft.material: Soft transparent guide material, never a photoreal electron cloud.

state_contract.model: Selected molecule with fixed idealized coordinates and independent guide visibility; methane tetrahedral, water bent using cited 104.5-degree schematic bond angle.
state_contract.authority: Domain state owns identities, values and accepted transitions. Derive labels and meshes from that state; camera and display offsets are separate.
actions: Toggle lone pairs and angle bracket.

invariants: Water always has two bonded hydrogens; guide visibility never adds atoms.
Camera motion never changes measured bond angle.
motion_guidance: Avoid morphing methane atoms into water atoms; transition through distinct named models.
Renderer tooling owns cylinders, labels and picking; molecule connectivity is authoritative data.
known_limits: VSEPR illustration, not electron density, molecular dynamics or an experimentally fitted structure.
Display radii and bond lengths are not van der Waals or measured values unless separately supplied.
Authored recipe only; runtime and rendered geometry checks have not run.

claims.statement: Methane has tetrahedral molecular geometry. Water has tetrahedral electron-pair geometry but bent molecular geometry, with a bond angle about 104.5 degrees.
claims.scope: Introductory idealized VSEPR comparison of CH4 and H2O; no quantitative electronic-structure claim.

colliders: None; display spheres are not collision radii.
physical_contract.timestep: Use a declared fixed update step for changing model state; interpolate presentation only. Pause clears accumulated playback time.
checks: Count bonds and confirm water guide toggles leave atom count unchanged.
